input: This memo recommends that a three-month pilot of bearing sensors be carried out on 17 pumps at a cost of $44k, under the ownership of the reliability engineering group, before any decision is taken on a plant-wide installation. The decision on full installation will be held until the pilot results have been reported to the March capital review. Over the past 12 months, maintenance records show a total of 1368 h of unplanned downtime across the 180 pumps at the plant, with bearing failures accounting for 42% of the downtime hours, which highlights bearings as a particularly significant contributor. A sensor set covering all 180 pumps has been quoted at $392k installed, plus $78k per year on an ongoing basis. In a vendor trial conducted on a comparable unit, the sensors were reported to cut downtime by 19%, although it should be noted that this figure is a vendor figure and was not measured at this plant. The proposed pilot therefore offers a valuable opportunity to test the vendor figure on our own equipment at $44k, as against $392k plus $78k per year for a full installation. It should also be noted that spare-part lead times are unchanged by the sensors, and the pilot will not alter them either.
target: The reliability engineering group recommends a three-month pilot of bearing sensors on 17 pumps, at $44k, before any decision on plant-wide installation; the decision on full installation is held until the pilot results are reported to the March capital review. Maintenance records for 12 months show 1368 h of unplanned downtime across the 180 pumps at the plant, and bearing failures account for 42% of the downtime hours. A sensor set for all 180 pumps is quoted at $392k installed, plus $78k per year. In a vendor trial on a comparable unit the sensors cut downtime by 19%; the figure is a vendor figure and was not measured at this plant. The pilot tests the vendor figure on plant equipment at $44k against $392k plus $78k per year for full installation. The pilot pumps are drawn from the units with the heaviest recorded downtime, so the trial runs where the recorded fault burden stands. The group fits the sensors without a planned outage, records downtime on the same basis as the maintenance records behind the finding, and reports the pilot units against the rest of the pump population over the same months. A pilot result that matches the vendor figure supports full installation at the review; a result below it leaves the full-installation case unmade on the present evidence. Spare-part lead times are unchanged by the sensors, and the pilot does not alter them.
